pageCache.pageTitle: International School of Creative Arts (ISCA) | Art & Design Boarding School UK
pageCache.text:
International School of Creative Arts
International School of Creative Arts (ISCA) is an independent boarding school situated in South Buckinghamshire for 15-19 year olds wishing to specialise in art and design subjects.
Progression To Universities: Celebrating 100% Progression
By perfecting the art of portfolio preparation, ISCA has built a reputation for highly successful student progression to leading art and design universities around the world including University of the Arts London (UAL). In 2026 ISCA achieved a 100% progression success rate.
Click here to find out more about progression and our student destinations
ISCA Moving Campus - September 2026
We are delighted to share some very exciting news with you: ISCA will be moving to a new campus.
From the upcoming academic year, starting in September 2026, ISCA will be based at the highly prestigious Heathfield School in Ascot, a leading independent school and a member of the Mill Hill Education Group. ISCA will operate within its own dedicated teaching, studio, and boarding spaces on the Heathfield School campus, allowing us to maintain our distinct identity while benefiting from an exceptional shared environment.
https://www.heathfieldschool.net/
This move represents a significant milestone in ISCA’s growth and offers outstanding new opportunities for our students.
Read our latest Newsletter
ISCA Newsletter May 2026
Creativity Matters Dubai 2025: Overseas Exhibition
ISCA’s exhibition, Creativity Matters, recently took place at the Contemporary Art Works Space in Dubai and proved to be a tremendous success. Held throughout the month of October, the exhibition showcased an impressive range of student work across the various art specialisms taught at the school, highlighting their creativity, skill, and dedication. ISCA’s Executive Director, Colin Kerrigan, together with the school’s specialist tutors, also exhibited their own work, adding further richness and variety to the show. ISCA extends its warm thanks to everyone involved in planning and organising the exhibition, as well as to all those who came along to support and celebrate the outstanding creativity of our students.

pageCache.pageTitle: History of Art A Level | Critical & Contextual Studies | ISCA UK
pageCache.text:
History of Art: Critical and Contextual Studies (CCS) offers students the opportunity to study the development of art and design theory and history in its many changing forms. The emphasis of the course is on evaluating and interpreting works of art in their social and historical context. There is also a very strong practical element to the course. No prior knowledge of the subject or practical art experience is required. However, students who choose this subject must have a good level of English in all areas; listening, speaking, reading and above all writing.
The main disciplines are as follows:
History of art and design
Critical writing
Critical and cultural analysis
Research skills
Critiques and discussion
Bridging theory and practice

pageCache.pageTitle: Extracurricular Activities | Sports, Arts & Cultural Enrichment | ISCA UK
pageCache.text:
The School actively encourages students to engage in a wide variety of activities that build on both academic and personal development. These workshops organised by art experts and regular guest speakers from leading art and design institutions around the world.
Building on the arts-focused syllabus, students are also introduced to the rich and diverse cultural life of nearby London and surrounding areas.
Our close proximity to the capital facilitates visits to world famous museums, art galleries and artist studios. The visits include exhibitions, talks and workshops to allow students to engage with the subject matter at hand.
The combination of on and off campus social activities provides students with an opportunity to gain a better understanding of British culture, as well as introductory them to new interests.

pageCache.pageTitle: Creative Arts Programme (CAP) | Pre A Level Art & Design | ISCA UK
pageCache.text:
CAP (Creative Arts Programme)
Pre A Level (Level 2)
CAP offers students aged 15 a unique opportunity to experience excellent UK art and design teaching. Students are able to develop their understanding of art and design through engagement with the work of artists and designers, materials, processes and techniques. Solid foundation skills are taught across a range of specialist art and design areas and students complete work that can lead to a qualification for the Level 2 Cambridge Technicals.
CAP promotes a creative approach to critical thinking and problem solving in a supportive educational environment. This enhanced programme also incorporates elements of mathematical and scientific thinking within the art and design process. Linguistic skills are also developed through personalised English tuition.
The Programme is designed to prepare students for progression to the A Level Programme. It is specifically for students aged 15 who have a strong interest in the arts and are considering further study in areas such as fine art, fashion textiles, graphic design, 3D design or critical and contextual studies. It can be seen as a first step to an extended course at ISCA.
Fees Terms and Conditions

pageCache.pageTitle: Foundation Diploma in Art, Design & Media | University Preparation | ISCA UK
pageCache.text:
A Level + Foundation Diploma in Art, Design and Media
Skills and Education Group (SEG)
In addition to the A Level programme, ISCA offers a Level 3 Foundation Diploma in Art, Design and Media which is designed to equip our students with the essential skills required for university success. This opportunity is open to students who are in their second year of A Level or enrolled in the Portfolio Programme at ISCA.
The Foundation Diploma in Art, Design and Media is a well-rounded course that gives students in-depth knowledge in their specialist subject. ISCA possesses an extensive network of specialist tutors, thereby enhancing students’ chances for direct admission into a three-year degree programme. The course is delivered at the same time as the A Level programme, setting it apart from typical foundation courses and providing a time-saving advantage for our students. They will also avoid additional accommodation expenses, as they will reside on campus for the duration of their course.
Students who successfully complete the Foundation Diploma course will leave ISCA having gained two respected qualifications. They will also have access to the Central Saint Martin’s Creative Practice Programme, which runs from September to the end of January.
By perfecting the art of portfolio preparation, ISCA has established a strong reputation for highly successful student progression to leading art and design universities around the world, including University of the Arts London (UAL). In 2026 ISCA achieved a 100% progression success rate.

pageCache.pageTitle: Central Saint Martins Preparation Programme | CSM Access | ISCA UK
pageCache.text:
UAL Creative Practice Programme at Central Saint Martins
The UAL Creative Practice Programme is an exclusive programme which offers ISCA A level and Portfolio Programme students the exceptional opportunity to study at Central Saint Martins (CSM) for one day each week. This in turn gives an invaluable insight and experience of the expectations of higher education study.
The UAL Creative Practice Programme starts towards the end of term 3 of Year 1 and concludes in January of Year 2.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care & Student Welfare | Boarding Support & Wellbeing | ISCA UK
pageCache.text:
At ISCA we place great emphasis on each student's well-being and student welfare is carefully monitored by all staff. The strong and caring community spirit is further supported by House Masters, House Mothers and Boarding Staff who organise many activities for the students.
We believe in the importance of providing students with a variety of positive experiences that encourage holistic development. Outside of the academic curriculum, the recreational activities are organised on a weekly basis. Students have the opportunity to participate in different sports including circuit-training, football, tennis, basketball and swimming. A full calendar of weekly activities includes regular film nights and evening lectures.
In addition, dedicated Welfare Staff work to ensure that each student receives personal care and support. Along with Boarding Staff, they are available to help with school and personal matters should the need arise.

pageCache.pageTitle: ISCA Campus | Boarding Facilities, Studios & Creative Spaces | ISCA UK
pageCache.text:
Situated in over 20 acres of beautiful rural grounds in Buckinghamshire, our facilities include an indoor swimming pool, new sports hall, tennis courts and football pitches. We share the site with the Teikyo Foundation Japanese school.
All courses are located in our recently renovated building and operated entirely separately from Teikyo Foundation. The building accommodates a number of specialist art studios that are also available during after-school hours for students wishing to complete homework or personal projects. Extracurricular workshops also take place here. The campus also includes a 3D printer, laser cutter, printing press and new photo-media centre which offer great scope for realising ideas.
We provide our boarders with a supportive and nurturing environment while preparing them for independent living.
Boarders have their own comfortable single room with en suite facilities, as well as a study area and plenty of storage. A weekly cleaning service is provided. Laundry facilities and kitchenette are located on each floor.
The school environment is monitored at all times by experienced House Masters and House Mothers. Outside of the classroom and studios, many sporting and cultural activities are organised to enrich the boarding experience and foster a strong community spirit.
Boarding Principles and Practice

pageCache.pageTitle: Art & Design Curriculum | A Level Creative Arts Education | ISCA UK
pageCache.text:
Year 1
In Year 1 students choose the three subjects they wish to carry forward to the end of Year 2. The first two weeks of the Autumn term are designed to help students familiarise themselves with the choice of subjects before they make a decision.
The subjects will lead to A Levels at the end of Year 2. The options are as follows:
A third subject must also be chosen, which will lead to an A Level qualification at the end of Year 2.
Students who are very weak in English will be exempt from choosing a third subject. Instead, they will follow an English as a Foreign Language (EFL) programme to ensure that they achieve the level of English required for progression to university.
All Year 1 students complete a Personal and Professional Planning (PPP) programme aimed at developing the study skills and habits required for successful undergraduate-level study in Art and Design.
Fine Art
Graphic Communication
Fashion and Textiles
3D Design
History of Art: Critical & Contextual Studies
Year 2
In Year 2, students continue with the three subjects that they chose in Year 1 in order to be ready to sit the A Level examinations in May.
It is expected that by the start of Year 2, students can already demonstrate the level of English required for university entry (usually an overall IELTS score of 6.0, with a minimum of 5.5 in each of the four components).
As well as preparing for their A Levels, Year 2 students need to work hard at securing a place at university. This involves developing a suitable portfolio of work and a personal statement in preparation for an interview with the university of their choice.
All Year 2 students attend the Creative Practice Programme (CPP) one day a week at Central Saint Martins (Click here for more details). This programme is in addition to A Level study.

pageCache.pageTitle: Fashion & Textiles A Level | Fashion Design Course | ISCA UK
pageCache.text:
Fashion and Textiles enables students to explore the different areas of the fashion, textiles and clothing industry, equipping them with practical and vocational skills as well as developing their academic and creative potential.
The relationship between textiles and fashion and other creative disciplines is stronger than ever. Students are encouraged to work in an interdisciplinary manner combining knowledge from different fields to produce fashion and textile ideas. Students are expected to embrace both modern technologies and traditional techniques in the creation of samples and designs.
The main disciplines are as follows:
Fashion womenswear
Fashion menswear
Fashion print
Fine art textiles
Constructed textiles
Dyed textiles

Bringing Generations Together Through Creativity
This week our students invited Swarthmore Care Home to take part in a creative workshop with the residents, and it was such a meaningful experience for everyone involved.
The workshop was all about bringing different generations together through creativity, conversation and shared experiences. Our students had the opportunity to listen to stories, learn from the residents, and build connections outside of the classroom, while residents enjoyed socialising, being creative and meeting new young people.
Intergenerational experiences like this are so important. They help students develop empathy, confidence and communication skills, while also helping to reduce loneliness and create a sense of community for older generations. It was a really special day and we’re so grateful to have been welcomed so warmly.

ISCA Student Exhibition and Collaborative Performance Project
ISCA students are proud to present an exciting public exhibition and live performance project that showcases the creativity, confidence, and professional preparation at the heart of our art and design education.
Year 1 and Level 2 students have been working collaboratively in groups of three to produce a series of paintings exploring the artistic transformation from Cubism to Fauvism. These works were developed during Portfolio sessions at ISCA, encouraging shared research, experimentation, and critical discussion.
Students have taken full responsibility for curating their own exhibition at The Old Court Art Space in Windsor, gaining valuable real-world experience of professional exhibition planning and presentation. The exhibition is open to the public and will be on display from 5th to 28th February.
Building on this project, ISCA students will collaborate with Windsor College Performing Arts students to create an immersive artwork that brings painting and live performance together. The piece will evolve from a structured, analytical exploration of form and space into a vibrant and unrestrained expression of colour and emotion, reflecting the conceptual shift between the two artistic movements.
The collaborative workshop will take place on 23rd February at The Old Court Art Space, Windsor. The final performance will be filmed, and a recording link will be shared with parents following the event.
This project exemplifies ISCA’s commitment to developing confident, independent, and internationally minded young artists, equipped with the creative, academic, and professional skills needed to succeed in the global creative industries.

Success of the ISCA Foundation Course
As we reflect on another successful year at ISCA, we are delighted to share the outstanding achievements of our Level 3 Foundation Diploma in Art, Design, and Media.
Following our recent external moderation visit on 1 July 2026, we are incredibly proud of our talented students and dedicated teaching team. The official moderation report confirmed 100% approval from the external moderator, with 77% of students achieving Distinction or Merit grades, and certification fully approved for all eligible students.
Key Highlights from Our Recent Report
Exceptional Student Achievement
Our students demonstrated impressive creative skill and maturity across a diverse range of specialist pathways, including:
Graphic Design
Illustration
Fine Art
Textiles
Digital Media
Screen Printing
Photography
Thoughtful and Ambitious Projects
Students explored complex and meaningful themes through innovative creative approaches, from investigating psychological interpretations of dark fairy tales to examining social dynamics and family relationships through their artistic practice.
Outstanding Mentorship and Support
The external moderator praised ISCA's comprehensive assessment feedback and personalised one-to-one tutorials, recognising the outstanding support provided to students throughout the development and completion of their final projects.
A True Bridge to Independent Creative Practice
The course successfully achieved its aim of bridging school-based learning with independent studio practice, equipping students with the confidence, technical skills, and creative toolkit needed to progress into higher education and future creative careers.
External Moderator's Feedback
"Contextual research has creatively informed visual language and the development of ideas. Well-developed levels of skill and control with materials are demonstrated throughout."
We would like to extend our heartfelt congratulations to all of our Foundation Diploma students for their dedication, creativity, and hard work throughout the year. We also thank our exceptional teaching team for their continued commitment to supporting the next generation of creative practitioners.
